title: The Twice-a-Week Field Walk
summary: Most problems are cheap to fix when found early; a regular walk with a look under the leaves is the best crop insurance.
actions: Walk a zig-zag path through the field, not just the edge
Check 10 plants in 5 places; look under leaves and into the whorl
Scan anything unusual with Lafaek and note it in Farm Activity
Act when 1 in 10 plants shows a problem, not when the whole field does

sections.heading: How
sections.body: Zig-zag through the field twice a week, check 10 plants in 5 spots, look under leaves.

title: Keep Simple Farm Records
summary: Writing down what you planted, when, and what happened turns each season into a lesson for the next.
actions: Log planting dates, inputs, problems and harvest amounts in My Farm
Note which bed grew which crop for rotation
Compare yields between seasons to see what worked
Photos of problems help when asking for advice

sections.heading: What to record
sections.body: Dates, inputs, problems, harvest. The Farm Activity log in this app is designed for it.

title: Safe Use of Any Pesticide
summary: Pesticides are a last resort; if you use one, follow the label, protect yourself and respect the harvest interval.
actions: Try cultural and biological controls first (hand-picking, soap spray, crop rotation)
Only use products registered for the crop and pest, at the rate on the label — never more
Wear long sleeves, trousers, gloves and cover your mouth and nose; wash afterwards
Spray in the early morning or late afternoon, never in wind
Do not harvest before the waiting period on the label
Keep products locked away from children and food; never reuse containers

sections.heading: Before
sections.body: Try non-chemical options first. Use only registered products at label rates.

sections.heading: During and after
sections.body: Protect skin and breathing, spray in calm cool hours, respect the waiting period before harvest.

title: Weeding Early Pays
summary: Weeds in the first 3–5 weeks steal the most yield; two early weedings beat many late ones.
actions: Weed maize at 2 and 5 weeks after emergence
Weed when weeds are small and the soil is moist
Mulch after the second weeding to keep new weeds down
Leave pulled weeds to dry on the surface as mulch, unless they have seeds

sections.heading: When
sections.body: Two early weedings (weeks 2 and 5 for maize) protect most of the yield.

title: Harvest and Store Well
summary: Losses after harvest can be as big as losses in the field; dry fully and store sealed.
actions: Harvest grain when fully mature and dry weather is forecast
Dry on raised racks or clean tarpaulins, not on bare ground
Test dryness: a maize kernel should crack, not dent, when bitten
Store in sealed drums, jerry cans or hermetic bags in a cool dry place
Check stored grain monthly

sections.heading: Drying
sections.body: Dry on racks or tarpaulins until a kernel cracks when bitten.

sections.heading: Storing
sections.body: Sealed drums or hermetic bags, cool and dry, checked monthly.
